description: Owner can list, rename, and revoke devices; perform remote sign-out; configure the global retention default and per-device storage quotas; destructive actions (e.g., clear-all) require explicit confirmation and are permissioned to the owner.

requirements.description: The owner can view a list of all trusted devices showing device name, pairing date, last-seen timestamp, and online/offline presence. The owner can rename any device. The owner can revoke any device, which triggers immediate session invalidation and trust group removal as defined in REQ-P0-006. All device management endpoints are permissioned exclusively to the authenticated owner; no other device user can enumerate, rename, or revoke devices.
requirements.title: Device Management: List, Rename, and Revoke

validation.notes: Unit test: list-devices handler returns only devices belonging to the authenticated owner_id
Unit test: rename-device handler updates device name and persists to relational store
Unit test: revoke-device handler calls session invalidation seam before removing from trust table
Unit test: device management endpoints return HTTP 403 when caller's device_id does not match owner_id
Integration test: owner lists devices; assert paired Device B appears with correct metadata
Integration test: owner renames Device B; assert new name is returned on subsequent list call
Integration test: owner revokes Device B; assert Device B is absent from subsequent list call and cannot authenticate
Playbook: open Device Management; rename a device; confirm new name persists after page reload
Playbook: revoke a device; confirm it disappears from the list and a confirmation dialog was shown before action

requirements.description: The owner can perform remote sign-out of any trusted device from the Settings/Device Management UI, which invalidates that device's sessions without full revocation (the device remains trusted but must re-authenticate). The owner can configure the global retention default (Live, Held with TTL, Pinned) and per-device storage quotas in Settings. Destructive actions (clear-all items, revoke all devices) require an explicit typed confirmation dialog before execution and are permissioned exclusively to the owner.
requirements.title: Remote Sign-Out, Global Retention Default, and Storage Quota Settings

validation.notes: Unit test: remote-sign-out handler calls scenario-authenticator session invalidation for the target device without removing it from the trust table
Unit test: settings update handler persists global retention default and per-device quota values to the owner profile record
Unit test: clear-all handler requires a confirmation token in the request body and returns HTTP 400 if absent
Unit test: destructive action endpoints return HTTP 403 for any caller who is not the owner
Integration test: owner triggers remote sign-out on Device B; Device B's next authenticated request returns HTTP 401; Device B can re-pair and regain access
Integration test: owner sets Device B quota to 100 MB; upload exceeding 100 MB from Device B is rejected with HTTP 422
Integration test: clear-all action without confirmation token returns HTTP 400; with token all items are deleted
Playbook: navigate to Settings; change global retention default; confirm new items inherit the new default
Playbook: trigger clear-all from UI; confirm confirmation dialog appears and cancel preserves all items

title: Device Management & Settings
